# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82 (Bi-Vb Pc82)

**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining every year
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82, titled *Anuvassa* ("Ordaining every year"), establishes a rule concerning the frequency with which a nun may confer ordination: a nun who ordains candidates in consecutive years commits an offense requiring confession. The background story (*vatthu*) explains that when nuns admitted probationers (*sikkhamānā*s) into the order every year, living quarters were insufficient (*upassaya tath' eva na sammati / vasanokāso na ppahoti*) [Hüsken 1997]. Under the disciplinary framework, a nun acting as a preceptor (*pavattinī*) is restricted to conducting ordinations only every two years rather than annually [Hüsken 1997]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Ute Hüsken similarly observes that the narrative framing of Pācittiya 82 is closely paralleled in Pācittiya 83 [Hüsken 1997].
